September 18, 2026

Discharge petition reaches 218 signatures to force vote on Epstein Files Transparency Act 2.0

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @groundnews

A discharge petition led by Representatives Ro Khanna and Thomas Massie has reached the 218 signatures needed to force a House floor vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act 2.0, according to Khanna. The legislation would allow Epstein survivors to sue the Department of Justice and federal officials who withhold accountability, and would compel the DOJ to comply with investigations including the ongoing criminal inquiry in New Mexico. Separately, Judge Emmett Sullivan sided with journalist Katie Phang in her lawsuit against the administration, ordering the Justice Department under Todd Blanche to produce handwritten notes and other withheld documents by September 24 or face contempt of court. The House recess called by Speaker Mike Johnson also pauses Massie's effort to force a separate vote on releasing Epstein-related government records.

UN mission finds grounds to believe US strikes in Iran were war crimes

tags: war, legal
sources: @groundnews

A UN fact-finding mission said it found grounds to believe US forces carried out February strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports center in Lamerd, concluding both attacks were war crimes. Iranian officials said more than 150 people were killed at the Minab school, including about 120 children; investigators found the site was civilian with no evidence of military use and said the failure to update US targeting records amounted to more than mere negligence. The Lamerd strike killed or injured 22 civilians. US Central Command denied striking Lamerd, while an internal US military investigation reported by Reuters found American forces were likely responsible for Minab. The same mission concluded Iranian authorities committed crimes against humanity in their crackdown on protests that began in December, citing killings, torture, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearances.

Second Circuit rules border agents may search phones without a warrant or suspicion

tags: legal, privacy
sources: @aaronparnas

The Second Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that federal officers may manually search a traveler's cell phone at the border without a warrant, probable cause, reasonable suspicion or any individualized suspicion. The court classified such searches as routine border searches. The ruling applies as binding precedent within the circuit and is expected to be appealed to the Supreme Court.

JPMorgan abandons forecasting an end to the Iran war as fuel costs surge

tags: markets, war, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

JPMorgan's head of global commodity strategy wrote that for the first time since the conflict began the bank has no baseline view and cannot model the end game, saying nearly every economic red line has been crossed. Gasoline is averaging well above $4 a gallon and reaching $5 to $7 in some places, diesel is near $9.99 in some markets, ten-year Treasury yields are above 5% and oil is above $100. Separately, Saudi Aramco has informed at least two European refiners they will not receive crude next month after Saudi Arabia shut its east-west pipeline in response to attacks, breaking term contracts that normally guarantee monthly supply. United, American and Southwest also plan to cut cheaper, less profitable flights next year as jet fuel reaches its highest level in months, with United's CFO Mike Leskinen saying some December flights will not operate.

House breaks early for election recess, delaying Hegseth impeachment vote

tags: politics, defence
sources: @groundnews

Speaker Mike Johnson canceled Thursday's House session and sent lawmakers home for a recess running through the November 3 midterm elections. The move delays consideration of eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth introduced by Representative Thomas Massie over Hegseth's role in the war with Iran. Johnson denied the schedule change was made to avoid the vote, calling the resolution a publicity stunt that would immediately be tabled. Massie said leadership canceled the session because they do not want to debate the matter.

Super PAC plans multimillion-dollar pro-data-center ad campaign in battleground states

tags: tech, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

According to Axios, the super PAC Leading the Future is preparing to spend millions of dollars on advertising in battleground states ahead of the midterm elections to persuade Americans that data centers benefit them. The effort shifts emphasis away from AI regulation toward expanding data center construction. The group's funders overlap with donors to MAGA Inc and to the president's ballroom project.

Texas approves data center projected to draw more power than 35 states

tags: tech, energy
sources: @oafnation_actual

Texas Governor Greg Abbott has approved what is described as the world's largest data center, which would consume more electricity than 35 states. The facility would draw from the Texas grid, which has a record of strain and failure.

Report says ICE has lost count of miscarriages among detained pregnant women

tags: immigration, health
sources: @oafnation_actual

A report published Tuesday found that Immigration and Customs Enforcement has lost count of how many pregnant women in its custody have suffered miscarriages. Civil rights agencies raised alarms about ICE denying prenatal care to pregnant detainees, according to reporting in The Guardian.

Republican Rep. Salazar says Trump immigration enforcement has gone too far

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @groundnews

Representative Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida criticized the administration's immigration enforcement in a new reelection campaign ad for her Miami-area district. She cited July figures showing half of roughly 50,000 people detained had no criminal record and urged the president to reconsider the advice he is receiving on immigration policy, saying Hispanics who helped elect him in 2024 feel betrayed. Nearly 75% of her district is Hispanic and over half are foreign-born; the district voted for Trump by nearly 15 points in 2024.

Mike Lee moves to scrap Bears Ears management plan after monument shrunk by 91 percent

tags: climate, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Senator Mike Lee has begun a process to discard the Bears Ears management plan written jointly with the five tribes, using a fast-track rule that would bar any future plan from being substantially the same. The president cut the monument by 91 percent in July, the mining ban lifted on September 11, and 16 mining claims were staked within days on formerly protected land. House investigators are examining whether mining executives bought a record volume of their own company stock shortly before the monument was reduced. Polling cited shows 66 percent of Utahns want full protection restored and 82 percent say tribes should have a strong role, including 76 percent of Republicans.

Uranium and critical minerals drive push to shrink Bears Ears

tags: climate, energy, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Lobbying from mining interests is a central pressure behind reducing protections at Bears Ears, where significant uranium resources remain near Cedar Mesa and the Valley of the Gods. After World War II the Atomic Energy Commission became the sole purchaser of uranium, creating a market that drove extensive development in southeast Utah, including the Moki Dugway road built to move ore to a mill site on the Navajo Nation. Debate continues over whether uranium belongs on the federal critical minerals list, given that the United States already imports it at low cost from Kazakhstan and Australia. Navajo families exposed to earlier mining continue to contend with health effects and a compensation fund whose funding remains disputed.

More than 30 governments adopt fossil fuel reduction policies after Iran war price spikes

tags: climate, energy
sources: @groundnews

The International Energy Agency reports that 33 governments have adopted measures to shift from fossil fuels to electricity or improve energy efficiency in response to the war with Iran and higher oil and gas prices. Policies include incentives for electric vehicles, renewable power, heat pumps and energy-efficient buildings, and clean energy installed since 2020 helped countries avoid an estimated $36 billion in fossil fuel imports during the first five months of the conflict. Global greenhouse gas emissions still rose 0.2% in the first half of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, while worldwide investment in wind and solar fell.

Republican anger builds over Iran war costs and Strait of Hormuz closure

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican commentators and Trump-supporting farmers have begun publicly blaming the president for economic damage from the war with Iran. Commentator Tony Lauren questioned whether Iran was genuinely close to a nuclear weapon or whether the threat was overstated. Farmers said they received no warning before the military maneuvers aimed at controlling oil supply and the closure of the strait. Separately, commentator Bill Mitchell suggested audiences try veggie burgers in response to high beef prices.

Former Army soldier pleads guilty to paying troops for military secrets sent to China

tags: defence, legal
sources: @oafnation_actual

A former Army soldier pleaded guilty after prosecutors said he paid active-duty service members for sensitive military information. The information was transferred to people in China.

DOJ will not appeal ruling on suppressors and short-barreled firearms

tags: legal, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Justice Department reportedly will not appeal a federal ruling concerning suppressors and certain short-barreled firearms. The ruling does not nullify the law nationwide for all parties.

Questions raised over McConnell's fitness as he casts deciding farm bill vote

tags: politics
sources: @groundnews, @aaronparnas

Senator Mitch McConnell cast the deciding vote as the Senate Agriculture Committee advanced the Farm, Food, and National Security Act of 2026 by 12-11. During the roll call he appeared to initially say no before Senator John Hoeven leaned over and spoke to him, after which he answered aye; McConnell later wrote that he was proud to vote yes and hoped for bipartisan support on the floor. The 84-year-old returned to the Senate on September 14 after a months-long absence following a fall, pneumonia and a hospital stay. Additional footage of him at his car has renewed questions about whether he is fit to serve out his term.

Air Force major faces 128 counts after release to home detention

tags: legal, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

An Air Force major faces 128 criminal counts. The officer had previously been released to private home detention over the objections of prosecutors.

Navy commits $1.7 billion to barracks as housing partner faces family lawsuits

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Navy is undertaking a $1.7 billion barracks program covering more than 8,000 sailors. Its housing partner in the effort is also facing separate lawsuits brought by military families in Texas.

Marine cold-weather boots failed during Arctic training

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Cold-weather boots issued to Marines began falling apart during Arctic training. Subsequent inspections identified 538 workmanship failures.

Army opens new promotion path for senior sergeants filling first sergeant roles

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Army has created a new promotion pathway for E-7s already serving in first sergeant positions. The change allows those soldiers to receive the rank and pay of an E-8.
